s.t: In 509 BC the Romans expelled their last king, Tarquin the Proud.
They replaced him with a republic in which two consuls were elected each year.
The consuls led the army and presided over the Senate.
A consul could rule for life if the Senate agreed.
Former consuls then joined the Senate, where they kept great influence.

passages.correction: A consul held office for one year only.
repairs: A consul could be removed only by the people at the end of ten years.
Only one consul was elected, and he chose his own successor.

s.t: The Industrial Revolution began in Britain in the second half of the eighteenth century.
Coal and iron were plentiful, and canals and later railways moved them cheaply.
Cotton spinning and weaving moved from homes into mills driven by water and then steam.
Watt's engine was the first steam engine ever built.
Towns such as Manchester grew very fast as workers moved to the mills.

passages.correction: Watt improved the steam engine that Newcomen had already built, making it far more efficient.
repairs: Watt's engine ran on water power, which is why mills stayed beside rivers.
Watt's engine was invented in the nineteenth century, after the railways.

s.t: William Caxton set up the first printing press in England at Westminster in 1476.
Before then, books were copied by hand, which made them expensive and rare.
Printing made books cheaper, so more people could learn to read.
Caxton printed many works in English, including Chaucer's Canterbury Tales.
The First World War began in 1914 after the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand in Sarajevo.
Alliances drew the great powers into the war within weeks.
On the Western Front the armies dug trenches that stretched from the Channel to Switzerland.
The war ended in 1916 when Germany signed the armistice.
Millions of soldiers died, and the peace settlement at Versailles in 1919 redrew the map of Europe.

passages.correction: The war ended with the armistice of 11 November 1918.
repairs: The war ended in 1920, after the Treaty of Versailles was rejected.
The war ended in 1917 when Russia and Germany signed a peace.
